title: Edamame: protein, fiber, and nutrients

seo.title: Edamame: protein, fiber, calories, and nutrients
seo.meta_description: Cooked shelled edamame provides about 121 calories, 12 g protein, 5 g fiber, and 5 g fat per 100 g. A 150 g serving provides about 18 g protein.
seo.search_intent: Understand edamame nutrition and what a normal serving provides.

excerpt: Edamame is soybean harvested while immature. Cooked and shelled, it provides about 12 g protein, 5 g fiber, 5 g fat, and 121 calories per 100 g. A 150 g serving provides roughly 18 g protein and 8 g fiber, an unusually useful combination in one food.
content_html:
Edamame looks more like a green vegetable than a bean, but nutritionally it is soybean. That shows up immediately: it provides far more protein than most vegetables while still contributing a meaningful amount of fiber.

What shelled edamame provides

The edible portion is the bean. Weighing whole pods would be misleading because the pod is normally discarded.

NutrientPer 100 g cookedPer 150 g
Calories~121~182
Protein~12 g~18 g
Fiber~5.2 g~7.8 g
Fat~5.2 g~7.8 g
Carbohydrate~9 g~13.5 g

A 150 g serving therefore supplies about 18 g protein and almost 8 g fiber, enough to make edamame more than a garnish.

Why it has less protein than mature soybeans

Edamame is harvested before the soybean fully matures and dries. It contains more water than mature dry soybeans, so nutrients are less concentrated per 100 g.

It has not “lost” protein; maturity and water content explain most of the difference.

Soy protein contains all essential amino acids

Like other soy foods, edamame contains all nine essential amino acids. That makes it an especially useful plant protein source.

It also contains meaningful fat

Unlike cooked lentils or many beans, which are very low in fat, edamame contains around 5 g per 100 g. Most of that fat is unsaturated and naturally present in soy.

Folate, iron, and other micronutrients

Edamame provides folate, iron, magnesium, potassium, vitamin K, and other nutrients. Its iron is non-heme iron, so absorption is lower than for heme iron in meat; eating it with vitamin-C-rich foods can help.

Sodium depends on how it is served

Plain edamame is naturally low in sodium, but restaurant versions are often heavily salted. For the food itself, cooked edamame without added salt is the cleaner reference.

The useful takeaway

Edamame occupies a practical middle ground: more protein than a vegetable, less concentrated than mature soybeans, and still rich in fiber. It can work as a snack, side dish, or meaningful protein component of a meal.

faq.question: How much protein is in edamame?
faq.answer: About 12 g per 100 g cooked; a 150 g serving provides roughly 18 g.

faq.question: Is edamame high in fiber?
faq.answer: It provides about 5.2 g fiber per 100 g and nearly 8 g in a 150 g serving.

faq.question: Is edamame the same as soybeans?
faq.answer: Edamame is soybean harvested while immature. It contains more water and is less concentrated than mature dry soybeans.
